Thirdly, he also submits that the correct identity of the land has not been given in the plaint though there appears some khatian nos. and plot nos. as to the description of the land but there is nothing in the record to show that which survey attract the said khatian and plot nos. So, this type of identity is vague and indefinite and upon relying such vague and indefinite identity of land there is a. little scope for giving possession to anybody else. 

 13. Fourthly and lastly he submits that the plaintiff has filed the suit for recovery of khas possession for an area of .90 acres of land as described in the schedule of the plaint. In the first schedule, there is a description of .30 acre of land from plot No.68 of khatian no.10 of mouza Kaida. But the deed of gift dated 22.02.1972 will go to show that the father of the plaintiff gifted only .20 acres of land to his 5 daughters from the land of plot no.68 of khatian no.10. So, the plaintiff cannot claim .30 acres of land from plot no.68 of khatian no.10 and the Court will not a pa'ss decree for the land where apparently the plaintiff has no right, title and possession. Thus, he referring the above points and arguments submits that the trial Court rightly dismissed the suit holding that the suit was barred by limitation. But the appellate Court below on some erroneous view came to a wrong finding and conclusion that the suit is not barred by limitation. So, the judgment of the appellate Court below is liable to be set aside restraining that of the judgment passed by the trial Court. 

 17. He also submits that it is not comet to say that the identity of the survey related with the khatian and plot numbers of the suit land have not been given in the plaint. He referring the plaint submits that the khatian and plot numbers are related with the settlement khatian. In this connection he also submits that when the first record of right was started under the provision of Bengal Tenancy Act in some of the area of our country. The first record of right is known as C.S record of right, that is, Cadstale Survey and in some district the same survey is known as settlement khatian. In the area of Mymensingh the first survey is know as settlement khatian and the same has been given in the pleadings. He candidly admits that it is fact that in the schedule of the plaint there is no identity of the survey and the same should have been there and if it would have been their, their would have no scope to create any confusion and unwanted debit on this fact. 

 19. He also submits that it is fact that the father of the plaintiff had gifted .20 acres of land from plot no.68 of khatian no.10 of mouza Kaida but the plaintiff has been claiming .30 acres of land from the said plot number. In this connection he argued that the defendants are nobody but the co-sharers of the plaintiff, thus the by an amicable arrangement among the co-sharers has been possessing .30 acres of land from the plot no.68 of khatian no.10 and since from the said particular land the plaintiff was ousted by the defendants, the same has been included in the schedule of the plaint. 

 32. The learned Advocate for the petitioner also raised question as to the identity of the suit land as in his estimation there appears no identity of survey in the schedule Nos. l and 2 of the plaint. It is fact, that in the schedule Nos.1 and 2 of the plaint, the description of the land has been given articulating the khatian and plot numbers without mentioning the identity of the survey. 

 33. From the plaint it appears that the plaintiffs has mentioned the plot and khatian numbers corresponding to the settlement khatian in the averment of the plaint but the same did find place in schedule of the plaint. However, in my consideration for this reason a suit must not be failed. 

 34. The last point raised by the petitioner in this suit is that the plaintiff has claimed .30 acres of land from plot no.68 of khtain no.10 of mouza Kaida although the father of the plaintiff gifted on .20 acres of land from that particular plot. In answering this point the learned Advocate for the plaintiff opposite party no.1 submits that in an amicable arrangement among the co-sharers, the plaintiff used to possessed .30 acres of land from the particular plot. I find no logic to accept this argument, because them was no scope for having possession into .30 acres of land of that particular plot as neither the plaintiff nor her other sisters jointly got .30 acres of land from their father through the deed of gift in the year 1972 and the amicable possession of the plaintiff is a absurd story because the relationship between the plaintiff and the defendants are very much hostile in nature. So, in my consideration I find logic and justification in the submission of the learned Advocate for the petitioners that the /4- plaintiff cannot get any relief whatsoever in .30 acre of land from plot no.68 of khatian no.10 of mouza kaida. 

 impediment in taking the suit as a whole in favour of the plaintiff save and except the land of the plot no.68 of khatian no.10 of mouza Kaida. As it appeals from the materials on record that the plaintiff is a woman who got the suit land from her father in 1972 and when she was living in the house of her husband, the defendants who are nobody but the members of the same clan tried to grab the land in this or that way and as part of their said ill device they created a collusive and fraudulent Hebabil ewaz. dated 23.10.1983 and the plaintiff in order to protect her right and interest into the suit land filed Other Class Suit No.26 of 1985 and the said suit was decreed and against the said verdict appeal was tiled by the defendants but the judgment and decree of Other Class Suit no.26 of 1985 remained enact and the proceeding arising out of the said suit was ended on 27.01.2000. Thus, it appears that the plaintiff being a woman was in litigation with the defendants from 1983 to 2000, that is, for about 17 years for the suit land. Thereafter, whenever the plaintiff got the judgment in her favour finally in the former suit the defendants enmeshed her in the present suit dispossessing her from the suit land on 27.08.2000 and the plaintiff has been fighting with the defendants from 2000. By this time when the former proceeding was pending the defendants have created as massy as 7/8 documents in order to create more cumbersome and complication into the peaceful enjoyment of plaintiffs title into the suit land. The defendants left no stone untouched to deprived the plaintiff from the suit land creating obstruction and hindrance one after another. They have been chasing the plaintiff from 1983 involving her with the suits one after another encyclicals and the plaintiff has been fighting with the defendants to foil their such ugly brazen attempt to grab the suit land. 

 35. On a careful scrutiny of the impugned judgment I find that the appellate Court below rightly passed the decree in the favour of the plaintiff, but the plaintiff is not entitled to get .30 acres of land from the plot no. 68 of khatian no. 10 of mouza Kaida but she is entitled to get a decree for .20 acres of land from that plot. It pertinent to point out here that the defendants also admit the title of plaintiff into .20 acres of land from plot no.68 as it reveals from the Hebabil ewaz dated 23.10.1983, as the plaintiff admitting the title of the plaintiff into .20 acres of land in that particular plot created the deed. So, in my consideration, the decree passed by the appellate Court below may be affirmed subject to modification in respect of quantity of land from plot no.68 of khatian no.10 of mouza Kaida. 

 36. In the result, the Rule is discharged. The judgment and decree passed by the appellate Court below is modified. The plaintiff will get khas possession into .10 acres of land in plot no.1452/85 of khatian no.458 and into .20 acres of land of plot no.68 of khatian no.10 of mouza Kaida and also into .30 acres of land in plot no.10 of khatian 106, into .09 acres of land in plot no.45 of -khatian no.108 and into .11 acres of land in plot no.49 of khatian no.108 of mouza Bajardi, that is, the plaintiffs suit be decreed for an area of .80 acres of land in stead of .90 acres of land. She will get the recovery of khas possession of the land specified in the schedule Nos.' and 2 of the plaint within the given boundary subject to the above modification.
